title: Molecular completion: consumptive signals, cis/trans delivery and renewal budgets
status_authority: Whole supplied source at its stated assumptions and read scopes; no Capital science execution, physical qualification or new independent audit.
reported_status: ROOT derives introduced coupled cis/trans delivery and quench models for a retained key, and a distinct first-hit model conditional on permanent destruction after the first cut. Selective quenching and sufficiently stable sequestration can each control modeled transfer only under their own unconstructed requirements. Destruction limits repeated transfer but not the first wrong target, false substrates or wrong chemistry. Stock and per-event lifetime calculations preserve the complete manufacturing boundary. No qualified chemistry, detector, local register, renewable factory or advantage is established; earlier N1822 results remain at their recorded scopes.
scientific_scope_status: ROOT derives introduced coupled cis/trans delivery and quench models for a retained key, and a distinct first-hit model conditional on permanent destruction after the first cut. Selective quenching and sufficiently stable sequestration can each control modeled transfer only under their own unconstructed requirements. Destruction limits repeated transfer but not the first wrong target, false substrates or wrong chemistry. Stock and per-event lifetime calculations preserve the complete manufacturing boundary. No qualified chemistry, detector, local register, renewable factory or advantage is established; earlier N1822 results remain at their recorded scopes. Actual product retention, chemical selectivity, donor clearance, cleavage topology, local delivery, fragment inactivation and end-group regeneration are separate operations. The supplied finite-state model assumes introduced k_cis, b, mu, c, alpha, W and correct fraction g; the one-use model additionally assumes permanently inactive fragments after the first cut. Uniform-sphere effective molarity is geometric, not a measured intramolecular rate.

proof_availability.classification_scope: A one-use key can still make its first cut on the wrong site. Faster indiscriminate trapping can destroy useful progression; stable sequestration is an alternative in the model rather than a demonstrated component. New source failures do not erase prior successful exposure or turn producer reports into ROOT governing reads. Per-event loss is distinct from per-cycle loss. Existing full-library, chemistry, assay, function, renewal and cost gaps remain open.
